reportText: @ Canyon Mouth , 28 cfs @ Fort Collins , 2 c fs @ North Fork below Seaman Reservoir Fall is here and the Poudre is in great shape! With the colder weather and precipitation we have been seeing the past couple of weeks, the fish on the Poudre have definitely been happy. Don't let the low flows scare you off, as there is still plenty of great opportunity up the canyon. As far as the fishing goes, we are pretty much on our winter program with where are flows are at. The Poudre is running low and clear, so keeping your presentation small and running light tippet is key to success. Running a small dry dropper rig has been effective on the warmer days when fish are actively eating midges and blue wings. On those colder days. running a deeper nymph rig with a small attractor like a prince nymph or hares ear with a small midge or blue wing trailing behind has been the way to go. The streamer fishing has also been great as the weather gets colder. Stripping a small thin mint or black wooly bugger has been a super fun way to find fish. We have been seeing the beginning of some spawning behavior in the canyon. Be aware of spawning fish and stay off of the Redds! Here is more information and what a redd is and how to avoid them! If you have any questions or are interested in booking a guided trip on the Poudre, feel free to give either shop a call. We'll be happy to help you get set up for a great day on the water.
